notes: Session 2. Both human-ordered items now closed: B5-0623 finished the heartbeat migration first, B5-0624 fixed the run-queue suffix crash second. B5-0624 was a LATENT crash rather than a live one, and that distinction was the task: [int] on a stripped task id throws for the B5-nnnnX class at two sites, the Sort-Object key and the lane-assignment site, so any OPEN suffixed row would take the whole runner down rather than failing one task. No OPEN suffixed row exists today because every suffixed row on disk (B5-0202c, B5-0329a, B5-0330a, B5-0331a) is DONE and filtered before the cast, so the runner is green and stays green until someone seeds something like B5-0625a. Root cause is a half-done repair of the same shape as B5-0613, which taught the row PARSER the suffix class and left every numeric use behind: a parser that accepts a shape its consumer cannot arithmetic only fires on the day the shape is used. Fixed with ONE shared Get-TaskNumber helper at both former cast sites so the next consumer cannot reintroduce the cast, +19/-2 and nothing else; row regex, prereq and lane tables, the B5-0622 duplicate assertion and every heartbeat file untouched. THE MORE VALUABLE HALF, disclosed not hidden: my first helper used an UNANCHORED [regex]::Match($Id,'(\d+)'), which resolves the 5 inside the literal B5 before ever reaching the task number, so B5-0005, B5-0202c, B5-0329a and B5-0621 ALL scored 5, the sort silently degraded to file order, and all five regression cases still reported crash=False. The assigned bug was fixed, nothing was red, and task delivery across the queue would have been silently mis-ordered. Caught by unit-probing the sort key before trusting the suite; corrected to ^B5-(\d+). Generalisation filed: a test that only asserts the absence of a symptom will pass a worse replacement, so the suite now asserts the PICKED TASK ID rather than the exit code. Verified: unit probe across eight inputs plus a four-row sort returning exactly the expected order, then six regression cases PASS against an isolated synthetic ledger in a temp dir with the live ledger never used as a fixture, and the live ledger -DryRun exits 0 offering the same head task as before. Gates green: compile.bat Build successful, runner exit 0 with no crash and no duplicate warning, heartbeats 27/27 conforming. B5-0621 remains OPEN and claimable for another agent. Reusable lesson: when a fix removes a symptom, assert the VALUE the code produces, not the absence of the error.
